Roofing in Galveston, TX

On the island a new roof answers to the city, the state windstorm program and, in four historic districts, the Landmark Commission. Call one free number at any hour to reach an independent roofing company that takes Galveston calls.

An island where every roof is a coastal roof

Roofing in Galveston, TX is not the same job as roofing in the suburbs north of the causeway. The whole island sits inside the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area, salt spray rides in on the Gulf breeze, and some of the oldest houses in greater Houston stand inside local historic districts with their own review for roof materials.

That means a Galveston re-roof usually involves three things beyond shingles and nails: a city permit, a state windstorm inspection while the roof is going on, and, on many blocks of the East End and Silk Stocking, a Landmark Commission review before any old roofing comes off. A roofer that works the island regularly will know all three. One that drove down from the mainland for the week may not.

Houston Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofing company. Call any time of day or night; an automated assistant gets the gist of the problem and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Galveston calls. That company inspects, quotes and does the work.

Roofing services Galveston homeowners ask about

Most island calls come after wind. A gust that peels a row of shingles on a raised beach house, a metal panel that started to rattle, a leak that only shows up in sideways rain off the Gulf. Older houses in town bring their own questions about decking, flashing at chimneys and what the Landmark Commission will accept.

Which Galveston roof job needs what

Three offices can have a say in a Galveston roof. This table sums up what each one has published; ask the roofer, and the city when in doubt, before work starts.

The jobCity of GalvestonTDI windstorm programLandmark Commission
Full roof replacementBuilding permit through the ePortal; the city requires the TDI WPI-8 when the replacement is finishedInspection during installation and a WPI-8 certificateCertificate of Appropriateness if the house is in a local historic district
Repair over 100 square feet, or any repair that replaces deckingAsk the Building Division whether a permit appliesTreated like other windstorm work: inspection and certificateReview may apply if the work changes materials on a historic house
Small repair under 100 square feet, decking untouchedAsk the Building DivisionTDI says these small repairs are exemptRepairing original roofing in kind is what the design standards favor
Changing roof material (shingle to metal, metal to shingle)PermitInspection and certificateReviewed case by case against the Design Standards for Historic Properties

Questions about permits go to the City of Galveston Building Division at (409) 797-3620. The city says the property owner is responsible for making sure required permits are obtained, and that work done without one can bring double or triple permit fees and a trip to Municipal Court. In practice the roofer applies, but it is your house on the record.

The WPI-8, step by step on a Galveston re-roof

Galveston is unusual because the city writes the state certificate into its own rules: the Building Division says a WPI-8 from TDI is required on completion of all new construction, solar panels, siding and roofing replacement. So the windstorm inspection is not only an insurance matter here. It is part of closing out the job with the city.

  1. Before the tear-off. TDI asks that it be told about the project before work begins, using its application form WPI-1. Ask the roofer to show you that it has been filed.
  2. While the roof is open. A TDI inspector or a TDI-appointed Texas licensed engineer checks the work during installation, when decking, underlayment and the nailing pattern can still be seen.
  3. When it passes. TDI issues the WPI-8 certificate of compliance, and the city expects it at completion.
  4. If a step was missed. A Texas licensed professional engineer can inspect after the fact, and TDI may issue a WPI-8-E. That costs time and money a planned inspection would have saved.
  5. Check it yourself. TDI's website has a lookup for WPI-8 and WPI-8-E certificates. Search your address once the job is done.

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), most roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way (TDI exempts repairs to less than 100 square feet of roof covering that do not touch the decking). When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

Historic districts: when the roof is part of the history

Galveston has four local historic districts. The East End, created in 1971, covers about 66 blocks. Silk Stocking, created in 1975, runs along 25th Street, which locals also call Rosenberg. Lost Bayou, designated in 1994, covers about 23 blocks and takes its name from Hitchcock's Bayou, which was filled in during the 1880s. Strand/Mechanic is the fourth, and the only one that is mostly commercial.

Inside those districts, the city reviews exterior work against its Design Standards for Historic Properties, which are based on the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation. Landmark Commission staff reports from recent years show how that plays out for roofs:

  • Original roofing that can still be repaired should be repaired, not torn off.
  • A replacement should be historically appropriate, and where records of the original roof exist, similar in size, shape, texture and color.
  • Metal roofs can be approved when they are detailed to fit the buildings around them, and composition shingle is offered as an option.
  • Rolled roofing is limited to flat roofs.
  • A decision can be appealed, but only by letter within 10 days.

The commission has approved some material changes and recommended against others, depending on the house. Before you sign a contract for a historic house, ask the roofer whether it has taken a roof through the Certificate of Appropriateness process, and check the current standards with the city's historic preservation staff. A change of material can also change the windstorm details, so both reviews have to agree.

Why Galveston homeowners call the line

Two sets of sign-offs on one roof

A city permit and a state certificate are both part of an island re-roof. Calling a company that takes Galveston work means talking to people who deal with the Building Division and TDI inspectors as a matter of routine, and you can ask them on the first call how they handle both.

A wind event at three in the morning

During Hurricane Beryl, Galveston's top gust reached 86 mph and the island had four straight hours of 70 mph gusts early that Monday morning, Fox Weather reported. Since an automated assistant takes the call at every hour of the night, you can describe the damage while it is fresh and get your details to a roofer.

Old houses with unusual roofs

Steep Victorian gables, turrets, box gutters and old chimneys need a roofer who is comfortable with detail work and with a design review. Ask about that directly when you are put through.

Nothing to pay the line

The call costs you nothing. You deal with the roofing company directly on price and paperwork, and you are free to get other quotes. Companies may pay the line a referral fee, and the line says so on every page.

Storms the island remembers

Hurricane Ike came ashore at Galveston early on September 13, 2008, at the upper end of Category 2 strength, according to the National Hurricane Center. Its report says the worst surge struck the Bolivar Peninsula and parts of Chambers County, where ground teams estimated the water at about 15 to 20 feet because many tide gauges failed.

Hurricane Beryl, on July 8, 2024, made landfall to the southwest near Matagorda but still swept the island with hurricane-force gusts. The National Weather Service's Houston/Galveston office reported numerous trees and power lines down across the region, and its highest gust, 97 mph, was measured near the Brazos River in neighboring Brazoria County.

After any storm, TWIA tells policyholders not to make permanent repairs such as a roof replacement until its adjuster has inspected, and claims must be filed within one year. Temporary steps to stop more water getting in are a different matter: ask your insurer what it expects.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Salt, sun and fasteners

Wind gets the headlines, but salt does damage every day. FEMA's technical bulletin on corrosion in coastal areas says salt spray is heaviest near breaking waves and drops off quickly over the first 300 to 3,000 feet inland. For exposed roof connectors and fasteners inside that 3,000-foot band, FEMA recommends hot-dip galvanized or stainless steel, and it discourages mechanically galvanized fasteners for exterior use, particularly on the coast. On a narrow island, a large share of homes sit inside that band.

Corroded nails, clips and drip edge do not always show from the ground. A roof can look tidy while the metal holding it down has thinned. That is one reason a Galveston inspection should include close photos of fasteners and flashing, and why a quote should name the metal for each part.

Raised houses and beach homes

The beach houses of the West End and the Bolivar side stand on tall pilings, which puts the roof higher off the ground and more exposed to wind than a slab house on the mainland. Getting materials and a crew up safely takes planning. Ask how the roofer will protect decks, railings and stairs while the work is under way.

Questions to ask a roofer about a Galveston roof

Paperwork

  • Are you registered with the City of Galveston, and will you pull the permit in your name?
  • Who files with TDI before work starts, and who schedules the windstorm inspections?
  • When will I have the WPI-8, and will you send me a copy?
  • Is my house in a local historic district, and have you taken a roof through the Landmark Commission before?

Materials

  • What are the nails, clips, drip edge and flashing made of, given how close I am to the water?
  • Which shingles or panels will you use, and are they rated for the wind speeds in the coastal code?
  • What will you do if you find soft decking, and what is the price per sheet?
  • Can you send me your certificate of liability insurance and a written workmanship warranty?

Not sure whether your Galveston roof needs a repair, a full replacement or a design review first? Call and describe the house and the damage. The roofing company you are put through to looks at the roof in person and gives you its own written estimate.

How a Galveston call works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Does a Galveston re-roof need a city permit?

Plan on it. The City of Galveston issues roof permits through its Building Division, which takes applications, contractor registrations and inspection requests on its online ePortal. The city also says a TDI WPI-8 is required when a roofing replacement is finished. The owner is responsible for making sure required permits are pulled, and the city warns that unpermitted work can bring double or triple fees. Ask the roofer to pull the permit in its own name. More on what a new roof should include.

What is a WPI-8 and why does my Galveston roof need one?

A WPI-8 is the certificate of compliance the Texas Department of Insurance issues when windstorm-code work passes inspection. All of Galveston County is in the state's designated catastrophe area, and the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses the certificate to decide whether a building can be insured. Most roof replacements need one; TDI exempts small repairs under 100 square feet that do not touch the decking. You can look up a property's certificate on the TDI website. See the roof insurance claims guide.

Can I put a metal roof on a house in a Galveston historic district?

Sometimes. In the East End, Silk Stocking, Lost Bayou and Strand/Mechanic districts, a roof replacement goes to the Landmark Commission as a Certificate of Appropriateness request. Staff reports show the city's Design Standards allow metal when it is detailed to suit the surrounding buildings, and they also favor repairing original roofing that can be saved. Outcomes depend on the house and its history, so ask the city's historic preservation staff before you sign. The metal roofing page covers panel types.

How does salt air affect a roof on Galveston Island?

Salt spray corrodes ordinary steel. FEMA's guidance on coastal construction says salt in the air is heaviest near breaking waves and falls off quickly over the first 300 to 3,000 feet inland, and it recommends hot-dip galvanized or stainless steel for exposed roof connectors and fasteners within 3,000 feet of the coast. Ask the roofer what the nails, clips and flashing are made of. The roof inspection page explains what a careful inspection should check.

Who will I talk to if I call about a Galveston roof?

First an automated assistant, which answers at any hour and asks what the roof is doing and where you are on the island. Then the call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Galveston calls. The inspection, quote and repair are that company's job, and it bills you directly.
